array-vs-arraylist.title: Arrays vs ArrayList
array-vs-arraylist.short: Choose between fixed arrays and resizable lists
array-vs-arraylist.summary: Understand the basic tradeoffs between Java arrays and ArrayList.
array-vs-arraylist.why: Arrays have a fixed length and can directly store primitives, while ArrayList provides a resizable collection API.
array-vs-arraylist.tips: Prefer arrays for fixed-size data or low-level APIs and List for ordinary collections that grow or shrink.

autoboxing-unboxing.title: Autoboxing and unboxing
autoboxing-unboxing.short: Understand automatic int and Integer conversion
autoboxing-unboxing.summary: Java automatically converts between primitives and their wrapper types in many contexts.
autoboxing-unboxing.why: Collections require reference types, so int values are boxed into Integer objects and can later be unboxed automatically.
autoboxing-unboxing.tips: Remember that unboxing a null wrapper throws NullPointerException.

collections-sort.title: Sort with Collections.sort
collections-sort.short: Sort a mutable List in place
collections-sort.summary: Use Collections.sort to reorder a mutable List.
collections-sort.why: Collections.sort orders an existing list by natural ordering or a supplied Comparator.
collections-sort.tips: Immutable lists such as List.of cannot be sorted in place; copy them into an ArrayList first when mutation is needed.

regex-pattern-matcher.title: Regex with Pattern and Matcher
regex-pattern-matcher.summary: Use Pattern and Matcher for reusable regular-expression matching.
regex-pattern-matcher.why: A compiled Pattern can be reused for multiple inputs while Matcher provides searching and captured groups.
regex-pattern-matcher.tips: Backslashes have meaning in both Java string literals and regex syntax, so escaping often needs two levels.

array-store-exception.title: ArrayStoreException
array-store-exception.short: Storing a value incompatible with an array's runtime type
array-store-exception.summary: Understand ArrayStoreException caused by Java array covariance.
array-store-exception.why: A String[] may be referenced as Object[], but its runtime component type is still String, so storing an Integer fails.
array-store-exception.tips: Avoid heterogeneous array designs and prefer generic collections when compile-time type checking fits the problem.

negative-array-size-exception.title: NegativeArraySizeException
negative-array-size-exception.short: Creating an array with a negative length
negative-array-size-exception.summary: Handle failures caused by a negative array length.
negative-array-size-exception.why: Java array lengths must be zero or greater, so a negative runtime size causes NegativeArraySizeException.
negative-array-size-exception.tips: Validate external input and computed sizes before allocating arrays.

lossy-conversion.title: Possible lossy conversion error
lossy-conversion.summary: A compiler error occurs when an assignment could lose numeric information.
lossy-conversion.why: Java does not implicitly narrow values such as double to int because fractional data or range may be lost.
lossy-conversion.tips: Before adding a cast, verify that truncation and the target type's range are actually acceptable.

constructor-cannot-be-applied.title: Constructor cannot be applied error
constructor-cannot-be-applied.summary: This error occurs when a constructor call does not match an available parameter list.
constructor-cannot-be-applied.why: Defining an argument-taking constructor prevents Java from generating the implicit no-argument constructor, so calls must match an explicit constructor.
constructor-cannot-be-applied.tips: Compare the required and found parameter types and counts shown by the compiler.

serial-warning.title: serial warning
serial-warning.summary: A common warning produced by javac -Xlint:serial for Serializable classes.
serial-warning.why: An explicit serialVersionUID lets a class intentionally control serialization compatibility across class changes.
serial-warning.tips: Also verify that Java serialization is actually required, then manage the UID together with the compatibility policy.

autoboxing-null-unboxing.title: Unboxing null wrappers
autoboxing-null-unboxing.short: Avoid null Integer to int failures
autoboxing-null-unboxing.summary: Automatically unboxing a null wrapper into a primitive fails at runtime.
autoboxing-null-unboxing.why: Converting Integer to int requires reading the wrapped value, so a null reference causes NullPointerException.
autoboxing-null-unboxing.tips: Handle null explicitly before unboxing, or use a primitive from the start when absence is not meaningful.
